breakdown.evidence: JD requires Python, pandas, scikit-learn, PyTorch and warehouse SQL. The CV shows only SQL against a MySQL replica plus Excel and Tableau.
Two years as a Data Analyst plus an internship, well short of the JD's 4+ years as a Data Scientist.
Only SQL appears verbatim. Python, pandas, scikit-learn, PyTorch, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, feature drift and experiment design are all missing.
Few bullets include measurable outcomes; most describe responsibilities without metrics.
Summary, Experience, Skills and Education sections present; length appropriate for a junior role.

gaps.evidence: The JD requires strong Python with pandas, scikit-learn and PyTorch. The CV has none of these.
gaps.suggestion: Ask the candidate whether any coursework, bootcamp, or side project involved Python data tooling.

gaps.evidence: The JD requires at least one ML model shipped to production. The CV has no ML work at all, let alone in production.
gaps.suggestion: Ask if the candidate has trained any model end-to-end, even a small one, and where it ran.

gaps.evidence: The JD asks for 4+ years as a Data Scientist. The CV shows two years as a Data Analyst plus an internship.
gaps.suggestion: Ask whether the analyst role included any modelling responsibilities that could be reframed under statistical modelling.

gaps.evidence: SQL is present against a MySQL replica, but the JD asks for warehouse SQL (BigQuery, Snowflake, or Redshift).
gaps.suggestion: Ask if the candidate has queried any warehouse platform in a course or hobby project.

gaps.evidence: Statistical modelling and experiment design are stated requirements. The CV does not mention either.
